How a project moves

Most work at the firm comes from government bids. This is the path a design actually travels, start to site.

01
Bid & win — technical and financial documentation
02
Site dimensions & client program
03
Schematic design, floor plans in AutoCAD
04
Exterior in Revit, interior in 3ds Max
05
Engineering coordination & approval
06
Construction documents & site supervision

Selected work

Woldia Mesob One Center Finished
Woldia — Governmental service center, 15 sectors, ~109 functions

Took a reinnovation project from existing-building survey through to a completed facade rooted in place — CNC-cut metal sheet panels referencing sorghum, the crop that grows around Woldia, set into a welded steel frame.

My scope: schematic design, construction drawings, 3D modeling, rendering, facade design, site supervision

Exterior render and Revit BIM cutaway showing interior office layout

Lalibela Mesob One Center Under construction
Lalibela — Governmental service center

Same building type as Woldia, but a deliberately different facade — white for elegance, brown drawn from the rock-hewn churches, integrated directly into the wall rather than applied as cladding.

My scope: design, drawing, 3D modeling, rendering

Facade combines white for elegance and brown drawn from Lalibela's rock-hewn churches

Woldia Playground & Football Field Under construction
Woldia — Public landscape, two phases

A children's playground built from raw contour data, plus the redesign of an existing, poorly-managed football field. A 60cm site level change became a design feature — folded into the terrain as a low hill rather than graded flat. Presented the finished scheme to the city mayor's office.

My scope: site analysis, landscape design, sanitary plan, construction documentation, client & contractor coordination

Football field and children's playground, rendered from the completed site design

Abay Investment Group Design approved
Bahir Dar — Facade & interior

My first fully independent interior — the meeting hall, modeled and rendered start to finish. Also my introduction to media facades: DMX-driven RGB strip lighting capable of color fades and video mapping across the building's face.

My scope: interior design, 3D modeling, rendering

Meeting hall — my first fully independent interior, modeled in 3ds Max and rendered in V-Ray

University & independent design work

Academic studio projects from Wollo University, alongside independent visualization studies — separate from the internship work above.

The Healing Home University — Studio
Hand-developed residential design

Designed for a cultural chiropractor and his family — wife and two children. The home embodies restoration, balance, and harmony, reflecting both the client's profession and Ethiopian cultural values.

Child and master bedroom interiors, developed alongside hand-drafted plans and a physical study model

Community Apartment — Kombolcha University — Studio
Kombolcha hillside, hand-developed

A community apartment on a hillside site with a 4-meter level difference and a connection to the water side. Instead of the horizontal expansion typical of the Wollo community, this project explores vertical living — saving land while preserving social interaction. Oriented for views, light, and ventilation, and finished in timber cladding that carries local cultural identity.

Hand-drafted plans, sections, and a physical massing model

Mixed-Use Tower University — Studio
Urban high-rise study

Integrates residential apartments, commercial space, and offices within a single tower, vertically stacking functions to maximize land use while keeping public, semi-public, and private zones clearly separated.

Agricultural Research & Training Center University — Studio
Kombolcha — Urban-agricultural campus

An integrated campus uniting research, education, production, and distribution within an urban-agricultural landscape. Architecture and landscape work as environmental systems, positioning agriculture as urban infrastructure for food security and community engagement.

Interior Studies Independent visualization
Home office, open-plan living, minimalist residential

A set of independent interior visualization studies — a home office balancing productivity and calm, an open-plan space blending lounge, kitchen, and wardrobe, and a minimalist residential interior built on spatial clarity and material restraint.

Rendering & Visualization Studies Independent visualization
Apartment facades & villa exterior

Independent exterior visualization exercises exploring facade rhythm and massing on a residential apartment block, and material contrast and landscape integration on a contemporary villa.

What the internship changed

Practical

Went from knowing Revit and D5 to modeling and rendering full interiors independently in 3ds Max and V-Ray, and from textbook BOQ to preparing real take-offs.

Coordination

Learned that a floor plan isn't final until sanitary, electrical, mechanical, and structural have all signed off — and that supervising a construction site means keeping seven trades aligned at once.

Communication

Presented designs to city officials, negotiated BOQ figures with a government contractor, and learned to explain a design decision to someone with no technical background.

Business

Sat inside the bidding process — technical documents, CPR, CPO, financials — and saw how a firm wins work before it ever designs anything.

Looking to keep working at the intersection of design, technology, and buildings people actually use.
